I just ran a PowerShell command to capture screenshots of the three test scenes (skylands, flatline, volcano) using the headless Edge browser. The command was:

```
$b = "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe"
Push-Location $env:TEMP
foreach ($m in @('skylands','flatline','volcano')) {
    & $b --headless=new --disable-gpu --window-size=1280,720 --virtual-time-budget=3000 --screenshot="scene-$m.png" "http://localhost:3000/test-scene.html?map=$m"
}
Pop-Location
ls "$env:TEMP\scene-*.png" | Select-Object Name,Length
```

The tool result returned nothing, which likely means either the screenshots were not generated, or the `ls` output was suppressed. Rather than re‑run the whole capture loop, the simplest next step is to run a `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) on `$env:TEMP\scene-*.png` with `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` to avoid noisy errors if the files are missing, and select the Name and Length properties so I can see if the screenshots were actually created and their sizes. This will give me a clear indication of success or failure and let me decide whether I need to retry the capture or inform the user.
